A dossier may narrow but never broaden its profile. All 118 IMPLEMENT_NOW, seven IMPLEMENT_TOOLING_NOW, and eight PREPARE_NOW cards use autonomous repository authority: 133 total. Nine VALIDATE_NEXT, two DEFER, one OWNER_ACTION, and one MONITOR card always remain outside the frozen autonomous release membership; their exact transitions may authorize only their bounded nonrelease, owner, or monitoring work.

<a id="v23-optional-capability-law"></a>
### 2.12 Required core and optional-capability fallback law

A required card may accept when its complete mandatory local core is green and an explicitly declared optional subcapability resolves to its exact typed disabled or manual fallback with zero public availability claim. This is not silent disabling. The fallback, reason, user-visible behavior, persistence behavior, and re-entry trigger must appear in `TypedAvailabilityAndFallbackReceiptV1`. This rule covers `DISABLED_NO_SELECTED_PROFILE` for an unselected adapter, a disabled rating link while Support remains available, dormant communications and measurement, unavailable on-device speech or authentication with the declared manual/recovery path, and optional encryption on a surface whose standard core remains complete. A required V23 card cannot use this law to omit its mandatory core, fake provider selection, or claim an unavailable capability.

P02-C10 is the sole declaration, generator, and lifecycle owner of `TypedAvailabilityAndFallbackReceiptV1`. It binds provider slice, consumer, exact candidate, availability enum/reason, mandatory-core result, user-visible copy/action, persistence and data disposition, fallback test/artifacts, public-claim scan, and re-entry trigger. Optional-provider rows consume this one type; feature cards do not redeclare it.

### 2.13 Candidate compatibility and aggregate acceptance

P00-C05 declares `CandidateAcceptanceCompatibilityReceiptV1` and `AggregateAcceptanceReceiptV1`; the active state-writer authority creates compatibility instances after independent verification. Compatibility context is the closed union `DIRECT_EDGE(sourceCardID,targetCardID,edgeOrdinal,directGraphDigest) | SELECTOR_MEMBER(selectorID,memberCardID,memberOrdinal,selectorDigest)`. Both variants bind the immutable original card receipt, unique canonical inclusion proof, matching `CardAcceptanceInclusionProofRecoveryReceiptV1`/currentness result, original head/tree, current candidate head/tree, ancestry result, governed path/contract/fixture/toolchain digests, every activated invalidation input, compatibility predicate/result, and any exact successor reproof. Only the selector variant feeds `AggregateAcceptanceReceiptV1`; only the direct-edge variant feeds `DirectPrerequisiteEvidenceSetV1`. It can carry a historical receipt forward only when every bound input remains compatible; otherwise the original stays immutable and a narrow successor receipt is required.

P00-C05 also owns `ConformanceReceiptV1`. Each receipt binds exact subject/set/journey IDs, subject and authority digests, candidate head/tree, applicable persistent/portable kind inventory, lifecycle/codec/hostile/interruption/recovery/compatibility or journey obligations, named evidence and artifact digests, exclusions, and zero missing/incompatible results. It is acceptance evidence only and never grants READY or implementation credit.

An aggregate receipt binds current candidate head/tree, selector ID and selector-row digest, ordered member IDs, original receipt, canonical inclusion-proof and matching proof-recovery/currentness digests, compatibility-receipt digests, successor-reproof digests, evaluator/toolchain identity, and exact `missing=[]` and `incompatible=[]` results. It accepts no code, grants no readiness or implementation credit, and cannot pretend historical card attempts shared one commit. P00-C05 is declaration, generator, and lifecycle owner; each selector consumer owns use of the generated aggregate at its exact candidate.

### 2.14 Nonrecursive receipt persistence and release integration

P00-C04 declares `OfficialAcceptanceDecisionV1 = ACCEPT | PRODUCT_FAIL | INFRA_PENDING | SUPERSEDED_NONPRODUCT`, its receipt, and generic effect recovery; P00-C05 owns `V23CardAcceptanceReceiptV2`, `CardAcceptanceInclusionProofV1`, `CardAcceptanceInclusionProofRecoveryReceiptV1`, and `ReceiptAnchorEnvelopeV1`. The exact ACCEPT predicate requires one reconciled PASS for every frozen gating cell, zero missing/skipped/cancelled/stop-fenced/unreachable/incompatible/quarantined/product/infra results, exact candidate/order/fence/artifacts, and released lanes. The controller persists the decision first; for ordinary cards the active state writer then applies exactly one generation-fenced effect. C04 smoke rejects every generic effect and uses its specialized transport/smoke effects. C05 uses generic recovery for PRODUCT_FAIL/INFRA_PENDING/SUPERSEDED_NONPRODUCT; only C05 ACCEPT uses pending controller quiescence plus `BootstrapFourWayStateAdoptionReceiptV1`. A card receipt binds the preexisting decision, attempt/order/completed fence, epochs, expected writer generation, and intended effect but never the later transition digest; the ledger transition binds decision+receipt+effect. The proof is a timestamp-free canonical function of the immutable historical transition, excludes the current locator/recovery actor, and is published/recovered as ABSENT/PRESENT/DIVERGENT before READY, compatibility, selector, aggregate, integration, or release credit. C05 stays pending after cutover until P00-C05 recovers its proof and only then may A00 finalize P00-C04 activation. Orphan or proof-pending receipts grant no credit, and proof recovery never repeats ACCEPT. Every receipt is immutable external content-addressed evidence bound to an already-existing candidate head/tree. A receipt is never inserted into the commit it names. An optional repository mirror may be committed only byte-for-byte as the sole authority-only change in child anchor `H`; it binds parent candidate `I`, is excluded from build inputs/product invalidation, and receives external validation. Later work starts from governed `H` when present while compatibility distinguishes evidence anchor from proved candidate. C04 mirrors only on phase and never advances main. P05-C01 remains external until `I` is fast-forwarded and identically verified on main; phase integration/P05-C02 bind `I`, and later evidence children never replace product/archive identity.

P00-C04 declares `ExpectedMainIntegrationBaseV2`, prepared drift/integration contracts, `C04CheckpointEffectReceiptV1`, `C04TransportActivationEffectReceiptV1`, `C04TransportActivationEffectRecoveryReceiptV1`, `C04SmokeDecisionEffectReceiptV1`, `C04SmokeDecisionEffectRecoveryReceiptV1`, `ToolingInfrastructureRepairAuthorizationV1`, and `C04PostIntegrationFailureReceiptV1`; it bootstrap-writes pre-C05 history under current A00 state-writer generation, and P00-C05 becomes canonical state writer/lifecycle owner only after byte-identical adoption. `ExpectedMainIntegrationBaseV2` has closed status `ACCEPTED_BASE | C04_TRANSPORT_ACTIVATION_PENDING | C04_TRANSPORT_ACTIVATION_INFRA_PENDING | C04_SMOKE_PENDING | C04_SMOKE_INFRA_PENDING | C04_CORRECTION_REQUIRED`. Checkpoint first sets activation pending. The decision-digest-bound transport effect atomically maps ACTIVATE to smoke pending, INFRA_PENDING to aligned infrastructure state/base, PRODUCT_PROOF_CONTRADICTION to CORRECTION_REQUIRED plus exact product/tooling repair authority, and SUPERSEDED to matching successor state; old/matching/divergent recovery prevents mixed branches. C04 smoke consumes an already-durable controller decision digest and atomically updates only state-writer-owned card state/receipt, postfailure receipt when product-caused, and base status. Drift intent binds exactly one live branch kind: `phase/v23-expansion` through first successful P05 integration outside C04 repair, `fix/v23-p00-c04-<signature8>` during product correction, `infra-fix/v23-p00-c04-<signature8>` under tooling-repair authority, or `release-fix/v23-<card-suffix>-<signature8>` after first P05 integration, where card suffix is lowercase `pNN-cNN`. Post-C04 phase drift rebinds C04 compatibility/reproof. Content-addressed receipt bytes are inert until expected-base CAS embeds them. Recovery is `BEFORE_EFFECT_AT_OLD_BASE | APPLIED_MATCHING_RECEIPT | DIVERGENT_OR_AMBIGUOUS`; crashes, replay, rewritten ancestry, arbitrary descendants, torn state, or unresolved impact fail closed.

Every C04 checkpoint, P05 phase integration, authority-only evidence integration, and postrelease fix first persists `IntegrationIntentReceiptV1` with exact kind-specific subject authorization and only legal child. Before remote-tip classification, retry searches immutable finalization/base/chain/incident history; an exact finalized match remains success when current main is that child or an accepted linear authority-only descendant with unchanged governed inputs/archive. Otherwise recovery is strictly old-base retry, applied-matching-child completion, or divergent quarantine. After C04 push/refetch, integration recovery creates only `C04CheckpointEffectReceiptV1(APPLIED_TRANSPORT_ACTIVATION_PENDING)`; enrollment/genesis/policy activation must close before trusted-default smoke. `ControllerActivationSubjectV1 = C04_CHECKPOINT | P05_PHASE` allows monotonic C04 correction/repair rollover under the same genesis and later P05 rollover; quota renewal uses separate `HostedCapacityEvidenceRenewalSubjectV1`. First P05-C01 ACCEPT atomically initializes `ReleaseTransportSelectionV1` generation 0 plus `ReleaseTransportRefreshAttemptAuthorityCellV1.EMPTY` epoch 0; a fresh accepted successor CASes only exact `SUPERSEDED(reason,authorityDigest,generation)` to the next generation. Every declared P05 invalidation atomically changes P05 state, selection, and matching refresh cell to its superseded/terminal variants with three-record recovery. Every initial/successor P05 integration atomically advances expected base and initializes/resets evidence chain to NO_CHILD at the new product tip through `PhaseIntegrationStateEffectReceiptV2`. It then remains HANDOFF_PENDING until that effect, policy activation, and enrollment rollover close. A deterministic postintegration proof contradiction supersedes all three P05 records; transient infrastructure resumes exact bytes. An evidence child receives only its authority-only integration receipt after push.

P00-C05 owns authority-only preflight/integration, `AuthorityOnlyEvidenceChainDispositionV1`, `AuthorityOnlyEvidenceIntegrationEffectReceiptV1`, redacted tagged `AuthorityOnlyEvidencePostPushViolationReceiptV1`, its exposure subtype, and typed incident disposition/resolution/effect recovery. NO_AUTHORITY_ONLY_CHILD applies only when main equals the current product tip; an accepted/rejoined evidence head requires exact TIP, and a tranche cannot consume its own receipt. Any post-push violation stops release; a disposition alone cannot rejoin the already-advanced main. Only false-positive finalization, approved forward remediation, explicitly owner-authorized history remediation, or release-blocking abandonment may close through `AuthorityOnlyEvidenceIncidentResolutionEffectReceiptV1`. P00-C04 declares/lifecycles candidate workflow proof, policy activation/evidence renewal, protected release transport, and rollover contracts; one P05-C01 evidence actor writes the workflow proof instance and P00-C04 validates it. P05-C01 owns selection initialization, epoch-fenced one-active-refresh authority, refresh authorization/fence/decision/recovery, monotonic selection, derived usability, and late-contradiction receipt. Time alone never mutates selection; only local-artifact P05-C02 effects require margin. Refresh waits for all terminal results, contradiction dominates success, and any authoritative late contradiction supersedes current selection/P05/refresh cell rather than being discarded as stale. P05-C02 hosted external mutation uses only the capacity-counted protected-release claim→mutation pipeline with an action-epoch mutation gate, unknown-effect reconciliation, and reachable post-start operational controls.



## 3. V23 additions and product refinements

### 3.1 Product refinements absorbed without parallel systems

#### Operational Party/contact/Site-role management

P03-C38 remains sole Party and Site-role-event owner and declares the exact `PARTIES_V1` and `SITE_PARTY_ROLES_V1` import descriptors. P03-C46 remains sole operational contact-point/handoff owner and declares the exact `PARTY_CONTACTS_V1` descriptor; P04-C42 owns editors and commands; P04-C31 presents handoffs. Commands create/amend/retire/reactivate Party, assign/end/supersede Site role, add/supersede/retire contact, and set/clear preferred contact with expected revision and atomic receipts. Duplicate names/values are warnings only. Retiring a Party with active roles requires impact preview and an explicit selected-role decision. Historical work/report/signoff/handoff snapshots remain frozen. No Contacts permission, CRM, communications history, or marketing conversion exists.

#### Response received elsewhere

P03-C48 adds `ReviewResponseAcquisitionKindV1`, closed outside channels, explicit `ORIGIN_USER_ASSERTION_UNVERIFIED`, immutable source wording, actor/time snapshots, and reconciliation. It requires an existing exported request and never fabricates a bearer proof or response file. Apply/history-only/discard/quarantine remain explicit. A later conflicting portable response preserves both facts and requires disposition. UI says “Response recorded” and “Not verified by AssetRounds,” never “Customer approved.”

#### Human-readable evidence details

P03-C06 owns `EvidenceDetailCardProfileV1` and the semantic projection; P03-C05 remains sole original/derivative provenance authority; P04-C04/P04-C02 provide setting, blocking detector, preview, and explicit `FinalAudiencePrivacyConfirmationV1`. The transform order is immutable original → audience privacy derivative → reviewed markup → readable details, followed by the audience-policy detector and user confirmation over the exact composed bytes. Any input or output change invalidates confirmation; export must byte-match the confirmed digest. Existing profiles default OFF. Details may include recorded time, explicitly user-reviewed capture time, frozen Site/Asset/caption/recorder display, role, and output-scoped reference. They never claim timestamp/location/person proof, never expose internal IDs/paths, never reintroduce prohibited data, and always have semantic-text equivalents.

#### Guided-template lifecycle

P03-C25 owns identity plus DRAFT/PUBLISHED/RETIRED events; published releases are immutable. Editing creates a successor draft; new work uses the selected published release; existing work never silently upgrades. Duplicate makes a new draft identity; retirement is non-destructive. P03-C18 supplies semantic diff/adoption. `.arsurveytemplate` import uses the one hostile archive/import engine and always lands as draft. Favorites and bounded recents are typed preferences, not analytics. No scripts, macros, generic EAV engine, marketplace, work answers, customer history, or unlicensed content enter exchange.

#### Accessible local signoff

P03-C38 owns exact purpose/subject/revision/disclosure, typed name, claimed role, actor/time, method, optional mark, and supersession. P04-C43 supplies one complete typed path and optional drawn mark and owns `SignoffEnrollmentManifestV1` plus its receipt. The minimum enrollment is `WORK_DETAIL_COMPLETED_RESPONSE_V1`: visible Work root → eligible completed-work detail bound to immutable `CompletedActivitySnapshotV1` revision → More → Record response → `SignoffEditorRouteV1` → focused `SignoffHistoryRouteV1`. A direct deep link cannot satisfy discoverability or FJ17. Recording creates no completion, approval, permission, authorization, or workflow transition. A mark is not biometric or required. An “approval response” is the recorded person's self-asserted intent, not AssetRounds verification or final approval. Signoff is a local recorded assertion—not verified identity, authority, acceptance for another person, legal signature/effect, nonrepudiation, workflow transition, or automatic Site role. Existing after-dark/safe-position acknowledgement records remain separate and byte-identical.

### 3.2 Competitive opportunities included in V23

#### Optional device-local App Lock

Opt-in, disabled by default, and based on `LAPolicy.deviceOwnerAuthentication` with device-passcode fallback. State is `DISABLED | LOCKED(reason) | AUTHENTICATING(attemptID) | UNLOCKED_FOREGROUND(sessionID) | INTERRUPTED_LOCKED | CONFIGURATION_UNKNOWN_LOCKED`. The unlocked session is never persisted. Real backgrounding, termination, or Lock Now invalidates it; transient inactive system sheets do not recursively prompt. Incoming files while locked receive size-only preflight and protected bounded staging; no parse/preview/index/apply occurs until unlock. The setting is device-local, excluded from workspace backup/export, cleared by Erase, and never described as database encryption or identity verification.

#### Passphrase-encrypted portable envelope

One `.arenvelope` wraps the unchanged deterministic backup/review inner stream. V1 uses NFC UTF-8 passphrases, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at exactly 600,000 iterations, a 32-byte salt, 32-byte key, AES-256-GCM, 1 MiB frames, random 8-byte nonce prefix plus big-endian UInt32 frame index, and authenticated canonical header/frame facts. File-provided arbitrary iteration counts are forbidden. Creation accepts exactly 15–256 normalized Unicode scalar values and at most 1,024 normalized UTF-8 bytes; preserve spaces/case, allow paste/AutoFill, require confirmation, store no hint/recovery/copy. App-generated outer filenames/share titles contain only a generic kind plus random public envelope ID—never inner/customer/work names or dates—and later user renames are outside app control. `frameCount` is exactly 1 through `UInt32.max`; even a permitted empty inner stream has one authenticated zero-length final frame. Indices are contiguous without wrap, exactly one final frame is last, and zero/missing/early/multiple-final inputs fail bounded structural preflight before KDF, allocation, preview, or write. Wrong passphrase and damage share one error. Validate every frame and hostile inner format before preview/write. Clear formats remain readable forever. P05 resolves Apple export-compliance metadata rather than assuming exemption.

#### Service-request intake

The primary path records a request received by phone, email, paper, in person, or other channel without requiring another app installation. Optional AssetRounds-to-AssetRounds invitation/submission files are Site-bound, single-use, cleartext in V23, and possession-bound—not monitored, delivered, authenticated, urgent, or safe for emergencies. The V23 envelope rejects service-request inner kinds; future encrypted service requests require a new released protocol. P03-C48 is the sole declaration, staging writer, and lifecycle owner of `PortableExchangeSessionStoreV2`; P04-C40 consumes it and cannot create a second store. Its atomic idempotent V1→V2 migration preserves bytes, IDs, timestamps, attempt/disposition state, and review capability protection; namespaces REVIEW and SERVICE_REQUEST have independent quotas, indexes, cleanup, and parser dispatch so exhaustion or corruption in one cannot evict, parse, or expose the other. Crash recovery resumes or rolls back from a journal. Backup/replace-restore preserves eligible sessions, clone/fork marks bearer exchanges history-only, and Erase removes app-owned staging and keys while acknowledging exported copies. Original subject/contact/urgency assertions remain immutable and unverified. Explainable same-Site/Asset candidates never auto-merge/close/create work. Conversion is an exactly-once separate mutation with immutable lineage. Status output is deterministic customer-safe PDF/text, not a delivery receipt or hosted portal.

#### Operational impact and qualified reliability

Users record observed impact rather than sensor-measured uptime. P03-C53 declares and lifecycles versioned append-only `QualifiedServiceExposureV1` input truth; P02-C01 remains its canonical writer, while P04-C09 alone owns metric definitions and output projections. Exposure records bind Asset, closed interval, time basis/zone, qualification source, coverage completeness, exclusions, revision/supersession, and correction lineage; reject inverted/zero intervals, overflow, cross-Asset references, and unresolved overlaps, and deterministically union valid intervals without double counting. Backup/restore/export/Erase preserve or remove them under the ordinary kernel, and projections rebuild solely from accepted events. Incident segments carry exact Asset, impact kind, planned/unplanned/unknown origin, observation/time uncertainty, cause assessment, repair/remedy links, restoration, corrections, and frozen subject context. Overlaps are unioned with FULL > DEGRADED > INTERMITTENT precedence. Open/estimated/unknown intervals remain visible but do not enter exact closed means. MTBF requires strictly positive qualified operating exposure and unplanned failure count; MTTR requires exact repair time and completed repairs. If qualified exposure is zero, availability and MTBF return `UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_QUALIFIED_EXPOSURE`. If only incident-to-restoration exists, label it mean recorded restoration interval. V1 availability is explicitly the percentage of complete positive qualified service exposure not covered by unioned exact UNPLANNED FULL_INTERRUPTION; planned nonservice is outside exposure, inconsistent planned overlap or UNKNOWN origin/impact makes it unavailable, and degraded/intermittent durations remain separate without invented weighting. No IoT, predictive maintenance, AI diagnosis, OEE, SLA, warranty prediction, or automatic release-to-service claim is added.

#### My Day

One bounded plan inside Today references existing work. It owns manual membership/order and an optional planning estimate only. Source owners continue to own due state, readiness, status, schedule, completion, and actual duration. At midnight/DST the old plan remains history and unfinished carryover is explicit. No dispatch, team assignment, route optimization, auto-prioritization, silent scheduling, or second work ledger exists.

#### Lightweight Parts & Stock

Parts & Stock is local recorded inventory, not procurement/accounting. Items use stable namespaced IDs/manual/scan locators and one canonical quantity unit. Storage labels are separate from customer Sites/LocationNodes. Balance is derived from append-only opening/count/adjust/use/return/transfer events and is UNKNOWN until opening/count. Adjust requires KNOWN and Use requires sufficient KNOWN source. Return is not a standalone positive movement: `StockReturnAgainstUseReceiptV1` binds one exact prior Use receipt/movement, same part/unit/work/material lineage, positive quantity no greater than its CAS-protected outstanding unreturned amount, and a KNOWN destination; free-form correction is a reasoned Adjustment. Transfer requires both sides KNOWN; UNKNOWN is never zero. Ordinary retirement requires known-zero everywhere, while explicit audited abandonment preserves unknown truth without asserting zero or financial loss. “Below preferred” is not an automated reorder. Explicit Use and Return atomically update stock plus the immutable work-material successor; compensation reverses its exact source effect. Concurrent/partial/double-return and idempotent retry tests are mandatory. Exclude purchasing, POs, vendors, valuation, tax, invoicing, payroll, serialized/lot/expiry, cloud sync, and replenishment automation.

#### On-device structured voice

Extend the existing speech/assistance architecture rather than introducing generative AI. Push-to-talk within a draft uses on-device recognition and a closed, versioned locale-aware grammar. Transcript spans explain every field proposal. Allowed fields are bounded descriptive text, explicit supported enums, number/unit, duration, and free material description/quantity. Diagnosis, compliance, severity inference, asset identity, schedule, stock decrement, canonical commands, completion, or finalization are forbidden. Per-field review is mandatory; audio is scratch-only; background/permission/capability failure returns immediately to a complete manual path.

## 4. Detailed V23 capability protocols

These protocols are normative expansions of the owning card dossiers. They define the minimum build; they are not optional examples.

### 4.1 Optional device-local App Lock — P02-C11 / P04-C16

#### Contracts and state

- `DeviceLocalAppLockSettingV1`, `AppAccessGateV1`, `AppAccessStateV1`, `AppLockReasonV1`, and `AppLockNotificationPrivacyDispositionV1`.
- `LocalAuthenticationClient` with the sole Release implementation `SystemLocalAuthenticationClient`.
- `LocalAuthenticationAvailabilityV1`, `LocalAuthenticationAttemptV1`, `LocalAuthenticationOutcomeV1`.
- `LockedIngressDispositionV1`, `PendingLockedExternalIntentV1`, and `AppLockRecoveryDispositionV1`.
- Closed state: `DISABLED | LOCKED(reason) | AUTHENTICATING(attemptID) | UNLOCKED_FOREGROUND(sessionID) | INTERRUPTED_LOCKED | CONFIGURATION_UNKNOWN_LOCKED`.

Launch order is minimal typed-preference load → blind content-free scratch hygiene → app-lock gate → successful system authentication → content-reading startup recovery → route restoration → canonical rendering. Pre-authentication hygiene may delete only known app-owned expired or crash-left scratch using trusted path, ownership, protection-class, and age metadata; it must not parse, decrypt, preview, index, deserialize, or derive customer/work facts. Ambiguous ownership or metadata fails closed and waits for authenticated recovery. This narrowly prevents protected crypto/import/voice scratch from surviving indefinitely when authentication is canceled without creating a content-access bypass. Cold launch, real backgrounding, termination, and Lock Now invalidate the in-memory session immediately. A transient inactive state caused by authentication or another system sheet does not recursively relock; the privacy cover remains active. Background during authentication cancels the LAContext and stays locked. Enabling and disabling both require successful device-owner authentication. A corrupt or ambiguous setting fails locked and may be repaired only after authentication.

The gate covers every root and route, resume/restoration, Spotlight, App Intents and Shortcuts, reminders and notifications, scans, incoming backup/review/adapter/CSV/share files, Support/Recovery, export, and share. A received file while locked may be bounded-size-preflighted and copied to protected staging, but may not be parsed, previewed, indexed, or applied. Expired staging is deleted deterministically. Existing private Spotlight entries are removed or reduced to generic actions when locking is enabled.

`AppLockNotificationPrivacyDispositionV1` closes system-preview leakage. Enabling App Lock records the existing canonical notification-detail policy, removes every delivered AssetRounds notification, cancels app-owned pending requests, and transactionally reprojects eligible reminders with generic title/body only: “AssetRounds reminder” and “Open AssetRounds to view details.” The request payload contains only a fresh opaque correlation token whose protected local mapping cannot be resolved until authentication; it contains no workspace, Site, Location, Asset, work, customer, schedule title, note, or route identifier. Every newly projected notification remains generic while App Lock is enabled. A tap gates before token resolution or route rendering, then validates expiry/workspace/revision after authentication. Disabling App Lock requires authentication, cancels generic requests, and idempotently rebuilds from canonical schedules under the previously recorded notification-detail policy; it never assumes detailed previews are permitted. Interruption uses a journal and resumes or rolls back without mixed private/generic pending sets. Erase cancels pending and removes delivered notifications plus mappings.

Exact copy:

- Setting: “Require Face ID, Touch ID, or your iPhone passcode whenever AssetRounds launches or returns from the background.”
- Disclosure: “App Lock limits access inside AssetRounds. It does not encrypt exported files, replace iPhone data protection, verify a person’s identity, or protect files after you share them.”
- Locked state: “AssetRounds is locked. Authenticate with Face ID, Touch ID, or your iPhone passcode to view local work records.”
- Face ID purpose: “Use Face ID to unlock your locally stored inspection and service records.”

Acceptance covers cold, background, manual, and terminated transitions; inactive system sheets; cancellation, lockout, not-enrolled, biometric change, passcode fallback, and passcode removal; corrupt setting; protected data; every route, intent, and document bypass; kill and relaunch around ingress; zero content in locked UI and app-switcher; enable with existing pending/delivered notifications, newly scheduled generic reminders, payload leak scan, tap before/after authentication, disable/rebuild under prior detail policy, interruption recovery, and Erase; VoiceOver, Voice Control, AX5, Reduce Motion, and focus; Release fake-client absence; and physical Face ID plus Touch ID evidence or an exact owner-hardware gate.

### 4.2 Portable-review trust correction — P01-C02 / P03-C48 / P04-C35

The transferable capability is exactly 32 random bytes from `SecRandomCopyBytes`. If repository hydration proves no accepted or escaped review-proof V1 bytes exist, `ReviewCapabilityProofV1` is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by that capability over this exact self-delimiting transcript:

`ASCII("AssetRounds.ReviewCapabilityProof.V1") || 0x00 || LP(protocolReleaseDigest) || LP(requestPublicID) || LP(requestManifestDigest) || LP(innerRequestPackageDigest) || LP(canonicalResponseBodyDigest)`.

Each `LP(x)` is `UInt32BE(byteCount(x)) || canonicalBytes(x)`. All four digests are raw 32-byte SHA-256 values, never hexadecimal text. `requestPublicID` is its released canonical ASCII representation with no NUL, Unicode normalization, case folding, braces, or alternate UUID spelling. The transcript has no whitespace or implicit string terminator. Verification reconstructs these bytes exactly and compares the 32-byte proof in constant time.

Normative vector RV1-001 uses key bytes `00..1f`, protocol-release digest bytes `20..3f`, request public ID ASCII `review-request-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, request-manifest digest bytes `40..5f`, inner-request digest bytes `60..7f`, and canonical-response digest bytes `80..9f`. The transcript length is 236 bytes, its SHA-256 is `5ab5c377885c524b13b17985b5782c34937ada353916c7861a7da97a23c0f0e6`, and the expected HMAC is `fb0b14df9c1bdbf6f19222ab40954b07a5c847eca3c5095a3cc379ff6fa5501d`. Checked-in tests also cover one-bit changes to every field and length, raw-versus-hex rejection, alternate public-ID spelling rejection, truncation, extension, and field reordering.

Hydration must inspect the released-data corpus before naming this framing V1. If any accepted or escaped earlier V1 proof transcript exists, preserve its exact reader and bytes under a frozen legacy profile, assign the framed transcript a new protocol/proof version and domain string, dual-read under explicit version dispatch, write only the new version, and add compatibility vectors; never reinterpret released V1 bytes. One capability is issued per request revision; the current proof version is single-recipient only in product intent, but copied request bytes copy response ability. The response carries only the proof. Clear inner-request re-export remains byte-identical; randomized encrypted wrapping does not create a new review request. The inner request digest—not randomized outer bytes—is the proof subject.

Closed capability lifecycle: `ISSUED_NOT_EXPORTED | EXPORTED_ACCEPTING | RESPONSE_PENDING_DECISION | HISTORY_ONLY_TERMINAL | HISTORY_ONLY_SUPERSEDED | HISTORY_ONLY_CLONED_OR_FORKED | UNAVAILABLE_CORRUPT_OR_MISSING | ERASE_PENDING | ERASED`. `proofValidity` and `applicationEligibility` are separate: a stale, closed, or cloned proof can remain historically valid but cannot mutate current work.

The sole capability copy lives in the exact protected internally retained request artifact, is eligible for exact workspace and device backup, is deliberately exported in the request, and is excluded from reports, open JSON, search, Spotlight, accessibility, diagnostics, logs, screenshots, support, marketing, and measurement. Replace restore continues the exchange. Clone and fork retain history only and cannot revoke already shared copies. Erase removes app-owned artifacts, sessions, and quarantine and cannot claim success while protected secret deletion is pending; it cannot recall escaped files.

Clear-request disclosure must explain that anyone who can open or copy the file can read it and create a technically valid response; AssetRounds verifies only exact-request capability use and post-seal integrity, not who responded, sent, received, reviewed, or had authority. Accepted response UI says “Response proof verified for this request” and marks self-entered identity unverified. Prohibited terms include verified customer, authenticated response, secure response, signed, and tamperproof.

### 4.3 Passphrase-encrypted portable envelope — P03-C54 / P04-C01 / P04-C35

#### Released format and cryptographic profile

- UTI `com.assetrounds.encrypted-envelope`; extension `.arenvelope`.
- Closed inner kinds: `WORKSPACE_BACKUP | REVIEW_REQUEST | REVIEW_RESPONSE`.
- Contracts: `EncryptedPortableEnvelopeProtocolReleaseV1`, header/payload/KDF/AEAD/frame types, seal/open plans and receipts, `PassphrasePolicyV1`, `EphemeralSecretHandlingDispositionV1`, `ReviewExchangeProtectionV1`, and `EncryptionExportComplianceDispositionV1`.
- Passphrase: Unicode NFC then UTF-8; creation accepts exactly 15 through 256 normalized Unicode scalar values and at most 1,024 normalized UTF-8 bytes; preserve leading and trailing spaces and case; no composition rule; permit paste, AutoFill, password managers, spaces, and Unicode; exact confirmation required. Readers accept every V1-valid value in that range.
- KDF: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, exactly 600,000 iterations for V1, 32 random salt bytes, 32-byte derived key. The parser never accepts arbitrary file-selected work factors.
- AEAD: AES-256-GCM, 1 MiB maximum plaintext frame, 16-byte tag, random 8-byte envelope nonce prefix plus UInt32 big-endian frame index. `frameCount` is exactly 1 through `UInt32.max`; an empty inner stream, if an inner protocol ever permits it, still emits one authenticated final frame with zero plaintext bytes. Zero frames are invalid.
- Authenticated frame facts: magic, protocol version, raw canonical header bytes, index, plaintext length, and final flag.

The clear header may reveal only envelope protocol and version, random public envelope ID, inner kind and version, KDF and AEAD profile IDs and public parameters, plaintext and ciphertext size, and frame count. It never reveals customer or work facts, internal IDs, dates of work, titles, addresses, notes, or capability bytes. The app-generated outer filename and share-item title are privacy-neutral and derive only from a generic kind label plus the random public envelope ID, for example `AssetRounds-Backup-<publicID>.arenvelope`; they never reuse an inner filename or include workspace, Site, Asset, customer, work title, address, or date-of-work text. A later user rename outside AssetRounds is outside app control. `frameCount` is exactly 1 through `UInt32.max`; frame indices are strictly contiguous from zero through `frameCount - 1`, exactly one frame has `final=true`, and it is the last frame, so nonce construction cannot wrap and every header is covered by at least one AEAD tag. Zero-frame, missing-final, early-final, and multiple-final envelopes are rejected during bounded structural preflight before KDF, allocation, preview, or write. Declared totals and counts plus integer and resource limits preflight before KDF. Existing P01-C04 stream is the plaintext; after full authenticated decryption, the hostile inner validator still runs before any preview or write.

Passphrases and keys remain memory-only, never in SwiftData, UserDefaults, Keychain, backup, draft, log, diagnostic, accessibility, screenshot, or test artifact. Discard them on success, failure, cancel, background, app lock, or memory pressure with best-effort buffer clearing and no impossible zeroization claim. Decrypted scratch uses complete file protection, no backup, search, Spotlight, Quick Look, or diagnostics, bounded capacity, and startup crash cleanup. No canonical mutation or preview occurs until outer and inner validation finish.

`EncryptedEnvelopeSealReceiptV1` and `EncryptedEnvelopeOpenReceiptV1` are secret-free, immutable evidence. They bind operation/attempt, protocol/profile releases, public envelope ID, inner kind/version, canonical header and encrypted-file digests, frame/size totals, generated neutral-filename result, source/destination protection classes, validation/test result, cleanup disposition, exact candidate/toolchain, and error category. They never contain a passphrase, derived key, salt-linked hint, plaintext/customer digest usable as a lookup label, raw inner metadata, or decrypted scratch path. Open receipt distinguishes only success, user cancel, resource rejection, unsupported release, or the shared wrong-passphrase/damage error externally; internal diagnostics remain nonsecret and noncustomer.

Backup offers “Encrypted backup — recommended” and “Standard backup”; both wrap or read the same deterministic inner format. A new envelope is immediately reopened and fully validated before share readiness. Review freezes `CLEAR_WITH_EXPLICIT_WARNING` or `PASSPHRASE_ENCRYPTED_V1` per request; encrypted request requires encrypted response with the same passphrase, no downgrade, and passphrase re-entry after background or relaunch. Legacy clear formats remain readable indefinitely.

Acceptance includes published PBKDF2 and AES-GCM vectors; deterministic TestSupport end-to-end vectors absent from Release; NFC, space, emoji, RTL, and long inputs; wrong passphrase indistinguishable from damage; one-bit mutations of every header, ciphertext, and tag field; zero-frame, missing-final, early-final, multiple-final, reorder, duplicate, omit, truncate, append, and oversize frames; integer and resource abuse plus unknown algorithm, profile, and version; RNG failure; oldest-iPhone KDF and maximum-file budgets; cancellation, background, app-lock, and protected-data interruption at every stage; crash cleanup; cross-device offline open; hostile decrypted inner content; clear-header, generated-filename, share-title, Files/Quick Look metadata, log, Spotlight, and support-bundle leak scans; secret-leak scans; legacy compatibility; and App Store export-compliance disposition.

### 4.4 Service requests — P03-C52 / P04-C40

#### Contracts and workflow

Use `PortableServiceRequestProtocolReleaseV1`, invitation, scope, submission, body, source, contact, urgency, media, and capability contracts, canonical local and external `ServiceRequestRecordV1`, import plan, disposition, and receipt, append-only disposition events and state projection, duplicate suggestion and decision, work-link event, status artifact, and exchange budget. `ServiceRequestSubmissionCapabilityV1` is exactly 32 random bytes from `SecRandomCopyBytes`. The sole origin-retained copy lives in the protected invitation artifact and the same raw capability is deliberately included in the exact exported `.arserviceinvite`; forwarding the invite therefore forwards submission ability. It is never copied into the submission.

`ServiceRequestCapabilityProofV1` is HMAC-SHA256 keyed by that capability over this exact transcript: `ASCII("AssetRounds.ServiceRequestCapabilityProof.V1") || 0x00 || LP(protocolReleaseDigest) || LP(invitationPublicID) || LP(invitationManifestDigest) || LP(frozenScopeSnapshotDigest) || LP(submissionPublicID) || LP(canonicalSubmissionBodyDigest) || LP(mediaManifestDigest)`, where each `LP(x)` is `UInt32BE(byteCount(x)) || canonicalBytes(x)`, digests are raw 32-byte values, and public IDs use their released canonical ASCII representation. The submission contains its public ID and proof but never the raw capability. Verification reconstructs the exact transcript and compares the proof in constant time. Proof validity and current import eligibility are separate facts.

The optional origin exports one single-use Site-bound `.arserviceinvite`, optionally binding one exact Asset or a small explicit safe target set. Recipient mode is entitlement-independent and isolated. Both `.arserviceinvite` and `.arservicesubmission` are cleartext in V23: the `.arenvelope` reader rejects service-request inner kinds, and adding encrypted service requests requires a future released protocol version. The UI says the exchange is readable and forwardable, not monitored, sharing proves no delivery, identity and urgency are unverified, and emergencies must use an appropriate service. Forwarding transfers the technical ability to submit. The recipient enters bounded text, date, urgency, and contact assertions and optional sanitized image derivatives, then exports immutable `.arservicesubmission`. The origin hostile-validates, quarantines, shows zero-write preview and duplicate reasons, and requires disposition. The primary path also records a phone, email, text, paper, in-person, or other request locally with an exact source label.

Closed import dispositions: `ACCEPT_AS_NEW | ACCEPT_AND_LINK_DUPLICATE | DECLINE_WITH_REASON | RECORD_HISTORY_ONLY | KEEP_QUARANTINED | DISCARD_UNIMPORTED`. Derived state: `OPEN_UNTRIAGED | OPEN_ACCEPTED | HANDLED_BY_LINKED_WORK | DECLINED | CLOSED_NO_WORK | SUPERSEDED`. `CONVERT_TO_WORK` binds request revision, target, package or activity choice, MutationID, and receipt; it creates zero or one canonical work link and leaves immutable request source history.

Exact same submission ID and digest returns the same receipt. Same ID with different bytes, wrong invitation, rebinding, or divergent response is quarantined. Multiple technically valid sibling submissions are preserved and require explicit disposition; acceptance of one makes that invitation terminal for new canonical admission but never deletes siblings or rewrites history. Domain duplicate suggestions require the same Site or Asset plus versioned explainable reasons such as exact category, normalized terms, or bounded window; no hidden score, fuzzy identity, automatic merge, close, drop, work creation, or AI triage exists. Both records survive; unlinking appends a reversal.

Only bounded JPEG, HEIC, and PNG-derived pixels are accepted; orientation is baked and EXIF, GPS, and metadata stripped. Mark `RECIPIENT_SUPPLIED_DERIVATIVE` and make no capture-time, location, or authenticity claim. Requester, contact, and urgency are self-asserted. Contact promotion is a separate previewed action and never creates marketing consent. The protected invitation mapping and immutable accepted source bytes enroll in backup/replace-restore and Erase. Clone/fork keeps request history but invalidates outstanding capabilities. Raw capability bytes never enter reports, logs, diagnostics, search, Spotlight, accessibility speech, screenshots, or support output; shared files cannot be recalled. Customer-safe status PDF or text may state a user-selected bounded status and note and proves no receipt or delivery.

Acceptance covers deterministic export and tamper; forwarding and two-device responses; replay and divergence; stale, moved, retired, or deleted Site and Asset; capability state; zero-write digest; concurrency and effect-before-receipt; exactly zero or one request and work link on retry; traversal, symlink, case, type, magic, compression, Unicode, and resource hostility; low storage, protected data, share cancel, and quota; backup, restore, clone, fork, delete, and Erase; leak scans; and VoiceOver, Voice Control, AX5, RTL, contrast, error focus, and draft preservation.

### 4.5 Operational impact and qualified reliability — P03-C53 / P04-C09

Contracts include `AssetServiceIncidentV1`, append-only incident events and state, `ServiceImpactSegmentV1`, impact kind and origin, restoration assertion, repair interval, cause assessment, failure-mode reference, remedy, incident-work relationship and correction, plus observation-window, coverage, exposure, metric-qualification, and input projections.

An incident requires one stable Asset. Impact is `FULL_INTERRUPTION | DEGRADED | INTERMITTENT | UNKNOWN`; origin is `PLANNED | UNPLANNED | UNKNOWN`. Each time fact separates effective or occurred time, recorded time, observation basis, and uncertainty. Impact transitions are segments, never mutable endpoints. Cause is `UNKNOWN | SUSPECTED_BY_RECORDED_ACTOR | CONFIRMED_BY_RECORDED_ACTOR`; the app never confirms it. Remedies reference canonical work. Restoration does not imply repair quality, safety, compliance, verification, or release to service. Continuation versus new occurrence is explicit, never inferred from time gap. Corrections append and supersede exact events. Placement, topology, package, and vocabulary freeze at the incident revision; replacement begins a distinct reliability identity unless an explicit lineage projection keeps histories separate.

Overlapping same-asset and function full interruptions are unioned. Mutually exclusive display precedence is FULL over DEGRADED over INTERMITTENT. Planned and unknown incidents remain visible but are excluded from unplanned metrics unless the versioned definition explicitly includes them. Open intervals show deterministic `asOf` state but do not enter closed means. Estimated and unknown bounds cannot enter exact duration metrics.

P04-C09 remains sole `MetricDefinitionV1` registry. It may publish recorded incident and active count, full and degraded duration, mean recorded restoration interval, mean recorded active repair duration, qualified MTBF and MTTR, and `QUALIFIED_RECORDED_UNPLANNED_FULL_INTERRUPTION_AVAILABILITY_V1`. `ReliabilityMetricProjectionV1` binds metric-definition digest, Asset and optional function scope, reliability-identity epoch, half-open observation window, `asOf`, numerator value/unit/source IDs, denominator value/unit/source IDs, sample count, coverage declaration and evidence IDs, exposure basis and evidence IDs, included and excluded event IDs with reason codes, interval-union policy digest, qualification status, unavailable reason, and projection digest. MTTR is exact repair time divided by qualified completed repairs.

V1 freezes one interval algebra for both availability and MTBF. Let `E` be the normalized union of complete, nonoverlapping `QualifiedServiceExposureV1` half-open intervals for the exact Asset/function/reliability epoch inside the observation window, after explicit planned-nonservice exclusions. Let `D` be the normalized union of exact-bound `UNPLANNED + FULL_INTERRUPTION` segments intersected with `E`; overlapping or touching segments form one maximal downtime component and retain every source incident/segment ID. Let `O = E \ D`. V1 availability is exactly `duration(O) / duration(E) × 100`. It may be evaluated only when `duration(E) > 0`; zero returns `UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_QUALIFIED_EXPOSURE` before division.

`QUALIFIED_RECORDED_UNPLANNED_MTBF_V1` uses exactly `duration(O)`—the same pre-percentage availability numerator—as its operating-exposure numerator. Its denominator is the count of maximal `D` components whose left boundary is an exact recorded transition into unplanned full interruption within `E` and the observation window. A component clipped from a failure that began before the window/exposure contributes downtime but no failure start; an overlapping incident beginning while already in the same component does not add a failure; a component ending and a later exact component beginning after positive operating time counts separately. Each counted component records its left-boundary event ID, all contributing incident/segment IDs, union-component digest, and included/excluded reason. An open component, uncertain bound, missing transition identity, ambiguous overlap, or incomplete coverage makes MTBF unavailable rather than silently changing the count. `duration(O) == 0` returns `UNAVAILABLE_ZERO_QUALIFIED_OPERATING_EXPOSURE`; zero counted failure starts returns `UNAVAILABLE_NO_QUALIFYING_FAILURE_STARTS` and is never infinity. The projection binds exact `E`, `D`, `O`, failure-start IDs, source revisions, interval-union policy digest, numerator/denominator units, and reconciliation proof that the MTBF numerator byte-for-byte equals the availability numerator for the same definition/window.

Planned nonservice must be removed from exposure; a planned interruption overlapping included exposure is an inconsistent-basis unavailable state. UNKNOWN-origin full interruption, UNKNOWN impact, uncertain bounds, incomplete coverage, replacement/reset ambiguity, or downtime exceeding exposure makes the percentage unavailable. DEGRADED and INTERMITTENT durations are displayed separately and receive no arbitrary weight in V1. App age, asset age, inspection and work count, and absence of recorded failure never imply exposure or uptime.

Exposure truth must be authorable and inspectable in shipping UI, not only test fixtures. The required entry is visible Asset detail → Service history → Exposure & coverage. A user can add an expected-service half-open interval, optional function scope, observation basis, declared completeness window, explicit planned-nonservice exclusions, uncertainty, and a bounded source note; review the timeline and every metric's included/excluded intervals; and append a correction or superseding interval without rewriting the prior fact. Inverted or zero intervals, overlap within one scope, exclusions outside the declared window, stale Asset/function revision, and incomplete gaps block qualification with a specific repair action. An unavailable metric links to the exact missing or conflicting exposure facts rather than a generic error. FJ09 starts from the visible Asset route, authors and reviews exposure, corrects/supersedes it, records the incident/repair/restoration chain, and then proves either a qualified projection or its exact truthful unavailable reason. A fixture-created exposure alone cannot satisfy journey acceptance.

Acceptance includes exhaustive transitions; all impact, origin, and cause states; restoration versus release separation; overlap union and precedence; DST, time-zone, clock rollback, and uncertainty; open `asOf`; concurrency and idempotency; meter rollover, replacement, reset, and incomplete coverage; zero, one, open, and excluded failures; golden formulas and unavailable reasons; asset merge, split, replacement, and move; restore, replay, delete, Erase, and rebuild; finalized-report immutability; 10,000-asset and high-event performance; accessibility and noncolor qualification; and scans excluding telemetry, prediction, remote monitoring, and collision with app-health `OperationalFailureV1`.

### 4.6 My Day — P03-C57 / P04-C41

Contracts: `MyDayKeyV1`, `MyDayPlanV1`, item, eligible-reference, estimate, carryover plan and receipt, source-state, readiness, and summary projections, and restore disposition. One plan per workspace, captured civil date, and time zone contains at most 50 stable references to an existing WorkPacket, RoundSession, schedule occurrence, or resumable work. It owns only membership, manual order, and optional whole-minute estimate from 1 through 720; source status, due, readiness, completion, cancellation, and reopen remain projections. Removal does not cancel or reschedule work. Planning estimate never becomes actual duration.

Midnight and zone changes preserve the old plan; carryover is explicit with a receipt. Schedule edits, superseded occurrences, completion, reopen, asset retirement, restore, and duplicate references reconcile visibly. Replace restore preserves exact plans. Configuration clone omits plans; workspace fork retains nonactive history only. Today shows Plan my day, source, due, readiness, estimate, manual drag and accessible move controls, existing Start and Resume routes, and collapsible completed items. An optional App Intent may open My Day but never read or mutate private work before the access gate.

Acceptance covers duplicate, cross-workspace, and stale references; maximum size; reorder and idempotent retry; estimate validation; midnight, DST, and zone adoption; explicit carryover; source edits, cancel, complete, reopen, and retire; interruption and relaunch; restore, clone, fork, and Erase; VoiceOver, Voice Control, AX5, and focus; and proof of zero auto-scheduling, route optimization, due-date mutation, or dispatch truth.

### 4.7 Parts & Stock — P03-C55 / P04-C44

Contracts: `LocalPartDefinitionV1`, stable namespaced IDs, stock unit and quantity, bounded `StockStorageLocationV1`, append-only movement and kind, use-on-work plan/receipt, `StockReturnAgainstUseReceiptV1`, frozen work-material snapshot, balance and attention projections, restore disposition, and feature policy. Storage has at most a top shop, vehicle, kit, or other label plus optional bin. It is not a Site or LocationNode. Each item has one canonical unit; EACH is integer, and other exact decimal units use at most scale 3. Unit becomes immutable after the first movement. Optional manual or opaque scan codes are stock-namespaced and never reinterpret asset QR payloads.

Balance is `UNKNOWN | KNOWN(exactQuantity)`, and UNKNOWN is never zero. Only opening count or physical count establishes or replaces a KNOWN balance. A reasoned positive or negative adjustment requires a KNOWN prebalance and produces KNOWN; it cannot initialize UNKNOWN. Work use requires a KNOWN source with sufficient quantity. Return is never a free-form positive movement: it must bind one exact prior `StockUseOnWorkReceiptV1` and source movement, the same part/unit/work identity and frozen material lineage, a positive quantity no greater than that Use's outstanding unreturned amount after all accepted returns/reversals, and a KNOWN destination. The outstanding frontier is CAS-protected so concurrent, partial, duplicate, or replayed returns cannot exceed the original Use or mint stock. A free-form positive correction is a reasoned Adjustment, not Return. Transfer requires KNOWN source and destination plus sufficient source quantity and updates both atomically. Any quantity-affecting operation against UNKNOWN fails without a movement; the user may instead count first or record an ordinary untracked work-material line that does not affect stock. No operation may silently produce a negative KNOWN balance. Preferred minimum drives an in-app below-preferred attention only, not purchase or reorder truth. Ordinary retirement requires every affected location balance to be KNOWN zero. An UNKNOWN balance blocks retirement until a count establishes truth or an explicit `ABANDON_UNVERIFIED_STOCK` disposition records actor, reason, affected identities, last movement frontier, and the fact that quantity remains unknown; that disposition is legal only from UNKNOWN, archives without asserting zero, and is never a loss or valuation write-off. A KNOWN positive balance cannot use that disposition and blocks retirement until transfer or a reasoned exact adjustment produces KNOWN zero; V23 has no positive-quantity abandonment shortcut. Referenced parts archive without rewriting history.

Explicit Use from stock atomically creates a movement and one immutable work-material successor under one mutation and receipt; compensation for an erroneous Use semantically reverses both. A legitimate partial/complete Return atomically appends one return movement, advances the source Use's unreturned frontier, and writes the matching work-material successor/reversal as applicable under one `MutationID` and `StockReturnAgainstUseReceiptV1`. Retry returns the same effect/receipt or no effect. Typing a material line never decrements stock. Configuration clone copies definitions only, with no quantities or history; fork history is nonoperational until recount; replace restore preserves exact truth; Erase removes it. Reports contain reviewed material snapshots only, never balances or storage. Feature disable preserves read, export, and recovery and blocks new writes truthfully.

UI lives under Work → Parts & Stock and contextual Use from stock; no root is added. Include search and filter, item detail, Count, Adjust, Transfer, Use, Return, Archive, drafts, exact `LOCAL_PART_CATALOG_V1` CSV import and export, manual fallback, low-stock view, and collision-safe scan. Return is offered only from an eligible Use/work-material lineage and shows outstanding quantity plus destination; there is no standalone unbound Return. Acceptance covers units, rounding, unknown, zero, and negative rejection; concurrent count/use/transfer/partial-return; idempotent and double-return rejection; use reversal versus return; atomic interruption/retry/reversal; retirement; locators; import hostility; search and rebuild; restore, clone, fork, and Erase; large catalogs/events; customer-output leakage; accessibility; and offline operation.

### 4.8 On-device structured voice — P03-C56 / P04-C45

Contracts: `VoiceStructuringGrammarReleaseV1`, field-alias release, capture context, field candidate, proposal quality and review plan, structuring adapter and closed registry, scratch disposition, and typed `StructuredVoiceProposalV1` under the existing assistance-proposal authority. V1 is deterministic; no Apple Intelligence, generative model, download, or server is required. Versioned aliases and locale-aware parsers are closed and fixture-tested.

Allowed proposals are bounded note, finding title and description, explicitly spoken allowed priority or condition enum, numeric value with unit, duration, and free material description and quantity. Forbidden: completion, finalization, compliance, diagnosis, severity inference, identity, placement, schedule, exact stock binding or decrement, and canonical command. Target is fixed at capture; a spoken possible part remains text until manual exact selection. Quality is `EXACT_EXPLICIT_GRAMMAR | AMBIGUOUS_REQUIRES_MANUAL_ENTRY | UNSUPPORTED`; speech confidence is informational only.

UI is an optional Speak details action inside an existing draft, with on-device recognition only, 60-second cap, visible recording, stop, and cancel, transcript and per-field cards with source spans, accept, edit, or reject, then ordinary draft save. It does not launch from background, wake, or App Intent. No cloud fallback or retained microphone audio exists. Unfinished active utterance may be lost on process kill; accepted field proposals checkpoint through C36. Manual entry remains immediate and complete.

Acceptance covers exact, ambiguous, and unsupported grammars; locale, unit, and number edge cases; permission denial and revocation; unsupported device, locale, and language assets; airplane and network denial; call, Siri, and audio-route interruption; cancel, background, and kill; stale target revision and callback fencing; audio scratch cleanup and Erase; no automatic write or stock mutation; Release network and model scans; accessibility, noncolor progress, and Reduce Motion; and parity of the complete manual path.

### 4.9 Manual operational contacts — P03-C38 / P03-C46 / P04-C42

Expected-revision commands create, amend, retire, and reactivate Party; assign, end, and supersede Site role; add, supersede, and retire contact; and set or clear preferred contact. Preserve exact display text; reject empty, control, and CRLF injection but do not destructively normalize international phone and email forms. Handoff viability is checked at action time. The first contact is not silently marked preferred; a lone active value may be used without writing preference. Equal values create warnings, never identity. Party retirement with active roles shows an exact impact preview and requires explicit selected-role termination; no cascade. Contact retirement never silently chooses a successor preferred value.

Routes live under Site detail, Party detail, and typed search; no Contacts root. Imported records use the same commands and editor. Legacy Customer or site name remains a Site label. Historical work, report, signoff, import, and handoff snapshots keep frozen values. Acceptance covers site-only migration; one Party and many Sites; many Parties with the same role; duplicates, preference conflict, and role overlap; stale, retired, and cross-workspace targets; injection; kill at every mutation boundary; effect-before-receipt; route and focus restoration; contact-free default export; and zero Contacts, marketing, or communications-history write.

### 4.10 Evidence details, template lifecycle, and signoff

Evidence details are OFF for migrated and existing profiles and deterministic for source, profile, snapshot, locale, brand, and renderer. Exact fields are recorded time, explicitly reviewed capture time, frozen Site and Asset display, evidence role, caption, recorder display, and output-scoped reference. Still-image copies may extend canvas but never modify originals; temporal media uses a normal text card. The transform order is immutable original → audience privacy derivative → reviewed markup → readable details. After composition, the system reruns the audience-policy detector and blocks confirmation on any prohibited fact. The user must then explicitly approve `FinalAudiencePrivacyConfirmationV1`, which binds source/profile/snapshot/locale/brand/renderer digests, the complete composed-output digest, audience policy/version, detector result, and previewed semantic text. Any markup, detail, audience, source, renderer, locale, brand, or byte change invalidates confirmation. Final export/share emits exactly the confirmed composed bytes or fails closed; a preview alone never authorizes output. Long and RTL content is bidi-isolated and wrapped; full semantic text exists beside any visual truncation. Tests cover unchanged original digest, transform order, detector blocking, confirmation invalidation, emitted-byte equality, stale previews and renames, hostile text, orientations and encodings, output-reference collision, semantic-tree parity, interruption and storage, and finalized immutability.

Template state is DRAFT, immutable PUBLISHED, or RETIRED. Editing published creates a linked draft; publish affects new work only; eligible drafts may explicitly adopt after semantic diff; incompatible facts block adoption without deletion or reinterpretation. Duplicate remaps IDs into a new draft and carries no work history. `.arsurveytemplate` import is hostile-validated, previewed, and imported as draft; same digest is idempotent, and identity and digest conflict requires explicit bind-as-update or import-as-new. Tests cover lifecycle, semantic upgrades, cycles, hidden requirements, rights, archive hostility, interrupted publish and import, accessibility, and proof that no generic script or EAV engine exists.

`SignoffSnapshotV1` freezes exact purpose, subject, revision, disclosure, typed name, claimed role, actor source, occurred and recorded time, method, optional mark, and supersession. A stale subject blocks Record until rereview; typed draft may survive. Primary actions are purpose-specific: Record acknowledgment, Record approval response, and Record change request. “Approval response” records the person's self-asserted intent only; it is not verified or final approval, identity, authority, acceptance for someone else, or a workflow transition. Generic Sign, Accept, Done, and Customer approved are prohibited. Typed-only completion and all assistive paths are mandatory.

`SignoffEnrollmentManifestV1` prevents an orphan component. V23's minimum required member is `WORK_DETAIL_COMPLETED_RESPONSE_V1`: from the visible existing Work root, open an eligible completed-work detail bound to an immutable `CompletedActivitySnapshotV1` revision; its More menu exposes `Record response`; `SignoffEditorRouteV1(subjectID, revision, purpose)` records one of the three purpose-specific assertions; success returns to `SignoffHistoryRouteV1` focused on the new record. P04-C43 owns the surface and enrollment receipt, P03-C34 owns route registration, and P03-C38 owns the schema/commands. The member creates no completion, approval, status, permission, or authorization transition. P04-C27, P04-C29, and P05-C01 are its exact closure consumers. FJ17 must start from the visible Work-root entry—direct deep-link setup cannot satisfy the journey—and prove entry, cancel/return, stale revision, typed-only and optional-mark completion, history/supersession, and restoration.

Tests also prove safety-acknowledgement compatibility, no workflow transition unless separately authorized, no biometric, identity, or legal claim, mark privacy and lifecycle, interruption and idempotency, backup, restore, and Erase, and fixed report and open-JSON history.



### 4.11 Security and trust-boundary summary

#### 4.11.1 Portable review bearer proof

If no accepted/escaped predecessor proof bytes exist, `ReviewCapabilityProofV1` is HMAC-SHA256 using a fresh 32-byte `SecRandomCopyBytes` bearer capability over `ASCII("AssetRounds.ReviewCapabilityProof.V1") || 0x00` followed by UInt32BE-length-prefixed protocol-release digest, canonical ASCII request public ID, request-manifest digest, inner-request-package digest, and canonical-response-body digest. Digests are raw 32-byte values. Detailed protocol §4.2 freezes the exact transcript, normative vector, mutation/reordering tests, and released-byte versioning rule. If earlier V1 bytes exist, preserve their exact reader and assign the framed transcript a new version/domain; never reinterpret released bytes. Verify in constant time. The response contains the proof, never the raw capability. Copying the request copies the ability to respond. Proof validity and current application eligibility are separate. Replace restore preserves the exact exchange; clone/fork makes it history-only; Erase removes app-owned copies but cannot recall shared files. The app must say that clear requests are readable/copyable and can produce technically valid responses; it never says authenticated, verified customer, secure response, signed, or tamperproof.

#### 4.11.2 Encrypted envelope limits

Encryption is an outer confidentiality/integrity option; it does not replace inner request binding or hostile validation. The clear header reveals only protocol/version, random envelope ID, inner kind/version, profile IDs/public parameters, sizes, and frame count. Passphrases/keys are memory-only and discarded on success/failure/cancel/background/app lock/memory pressure with best-effort clearing but no impossible zeroization claim. Protected scratch is excluded from backup/search/Spotlight/Quick Look/diagnostics and cleaned before normal startup after a crash. User-owned exported files cannot be recalled by Erase.

#### 4.11.3 App Lock limits

App Lock gates in-app presentation and mutation; it is not storage encryption, a user account, verified identity, role authorization, remote lock, or remote wipe. If device authentication becomes unavailable after enablement, fail locked and instruct the user to restore an iPhone passcode; there is no AssetRounds bypass. Release binaries contain only the system authentication client. Face ID purpose text is localized. Physical evidence covers Face ID and a supported Touch ID device when available; unavailable owner hardware remains an exact P05 owner gate rather than a simulator claim.

## 6. Common and feature journey acceptance

### 6.1 CommonTaskJourneyReleaseV2

P00-C08 is the sole declaration, artifact, and lifecycle owner of `CommonTaskJourneyReleaseV2` and `CommonTaskJourneyReceiptV2`. The release is the generation-rebound, no-loss successor to V21's canonical journey release. It freezes typed route, task identity, visible primary action, safe resume anchor, accessibility identity, exact starting fixture, checkpoints, branches, success endpoint, cancel/back/focus/fallback, and required evidence layers—not pixels. The exact ordered member union is:

| Stable ID | Frozen start and required semantic path | Frozen success endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| `J01_FIRST_ENTRY` | Fresh install or explicit Reopen setup → choose Start a new workspace, Try a practice round, Restore from backup, or Decide later; no first-launch permission request. | Chosen route or acknowledgment is durable and lands on stable Today, Practice, workspace, or restore state without replay. |
| `J02_REAL_WORKSPACE_CREATE_IMPORT_SELECT` | No selected REAL workspace → create, restore/import, or select through the one workspace authority. | One valid REAL workspace is selected and all four roots scope to it. |
| `J03_SITE_LOCATION_ASSET_CREATE_FIND_SCAN` | Selected REAL workspace → create or find Site/location/asset; scan may assist but manual lookup/entry remains. | Stable entity detail/work route resolves to the intended identity with no wrong-entity mutation. |
| `J04_OFFLINE_PREPARE` | Selected field work → run readiness and obtain required local references/content or an explicit blocker with remedy. | Receipt-backed offline-ready state, or truthful blocked state with actionable manual/recovery path. |
| `J05_ROUND_START_RESUME` | Ready or safely resumable work → Start/Resume → restore validated field/section anchor. | Active round is at the next required or previous safe item with durable checkpoint and no repeated effect. |
| `J06_EVIDENCE_CAPTURE_CURATE` | Active item → capture/import → durable stage → review role/order/caption/description → promote, Retake, Remove, or accessible reorder. | Curated evidence set is receipt-backed; immutable originals/history and required-evidence truth are preserved. |
| `J07_VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE_RESOLUTION` | Submit incomplete/invalid work → one submitAttemptID snapshot → summary/first invalid → correct or explicitly retain incomplete. | Validation is truthful, focus moves once, and no passive refresh fabricates completion. |
| `J08_COMPLETE_NEXT_CLOSE` | Completeness-eligible item/round → Complete & Next or close → canonical read-back. | Completion/finalization receipt exists and next item or stable closed summary is visible. |
| `J09_REPORT_PREVIEW_SHARE_EXPORT` | Completed snapshot → render/preview → choose share/export. | Preview/output identity is verified and journey stops at explicit system handoff without implying delivery. |
| `J10_BACKUP_RESTORE_RECOVERY` | Existing backup or recovery need → locate/explain → preview/validate → execute only the protocol-safe noncustomer step. | Verified backup/recovery result or truthful explanation/remedy; valuable customer data is never destructively exercised. |
| `J11_SETTINGS_ACCESSIBILITY_HELP` | Current productive surface or Settings → change one setting or open contextual Help → return. | Truthful read-back and return preserves valid route, draft, scroll, and meaningful focus; stale Help falls back visibly. |
| `J12_PURCHASE_RESTORE` | Owner-controlled App Store-signed Sandbox/TestFlight environment → purchase or Restore. | Store transaction/entitlement read-back is bound to tested build; simulated external effect never counts. |
| `J13_DELETE_ERASE` | Disposable noncustomer data → preview consequences → explicit confirmation → Delete or Erase. | Governed deletion/Erase receipt and absence/recovery truth are verified without touching valuable data. |
| `J14_PRACTICE_START_SWITCH_LEAVE` | Stable REAL/Today state → start Practice → switch/perform bounded task → Leave or Reset Practice. | REAL data remains byte/route isolated and return reaches validated REAL anchor or Today; Leave never deletes Practice. |

Every J ID requires automated semantic evidence. `CommonTaskJourneyReceiptV2` binds release/member digest, exact candidate head/tree, starting fixture, route/checkpoint/branch/endpoint results, cancellation/back/focus/fallback, accessibility layers, artifacts, and zero missing members. P05-C02 additionally runs J01–J11 and J14 uncoached, J12 with owner App Store-signed external-effect evidence, and J13 with owner physical disposable-data Delete/Erase evidence. No dossier may define a shorter common list, rename an ID, or replace its endpoint.

P00-C08 is the sole declaration and lifecycle owner of `FeatureEndToEndJourneyReleaseV1` and `FeatureEndToEndJourneyReceiptV1`. Each receipt binds the exact ordered FJ01–FJ17 release/member digests, candidate head/tree, starting fixture, real public-UI actions, checkpoints/branches/endpoints, accessibility/fallback layers, artifacts, and zero missing members. Planning never guesses file paths: hydration resolves exact paths/symbols from the accepted repository and constrains the card’s write fence.

#### Outcome and user value

Accepted S10.6 baseline and V23/V21 bounded delta, lineage, and accepted-brand lock. Produce one bounded, independently acceptable result while preserving every prior user-visible and data-survival behavior not explicitly corrected by V23.

#### Owned delta and constraints

Generation-rebind the semantic V21-P00-C01 outcome without loss. No independent feature is added beyond V23 relation, lifecycle, iPhone, brand/HIG, accessibility, localization, claims, and exact-candidate policy.

#### Inherited authority

`V21ToV23RequirementRebindingV1` incorporates only the semantic payload from `V21-P00-C01`: outcome, included behavior, exclusions, contracts, lifecycle, hostile cases, future-trigger/re-entry conditions, hard-stop boundaries, and acceptance criteria. It discards V21 generation, IDs, classification, dependencies, paths, branches, counts, current status, phase closures, and execution mechanics. V23 current metadata and corrections control. Source boundary: Appendix A from indented `### V21-P00-C01 —` through the line before the next indented `### V21-P` card heading or appendix end.


#### Explicit non-goals

The global V23 exclusion register is binding. This card may not create an unlisted root, store, writer, renderer, importer, identity source, network service, telemetry path, marketing conversion, verified identity, delivery, security, or legal claim, native-iPad surface, or neighboring feature merely to satisfy its outcome. Card-specific prohibitions in the owned delta and incorporated semantic predecessor payload are cumulative.

#### Persistence, interruption, and recovery

No new canonical product write is authorized unless this dossier explicitly says otherwise. Evidence and planning state remains outside customer work data and grants no implementation credit.

Every user-authored long form uses the universal checkpoint and draft authority. Every canonical workspace mutation uses expected revision, MutationID, one canonical writer transaction, durable receipt, semantic reversal or supersession, and effect-before-receipt recovery. Nonpersistent tooling, views, operating-system presentation, and explicitly device-local preferences instead use their declared idempotency and lifecycle contract; they never fabricate a workspace receipt. No optimistic UI may claim Saved, Complete, Sent, Delivered, Verified, Secure, or Approved beyond the accepted canonical fact.

External jobs are post-hoc occupancy evidence, never reservations/results; reconcile and debit them crash-safely, and block on unknown/uncontained occupancy. #### Explicit non-goals

#### Persistence, interruption, and recovery

No new canonical product write is authorized unless this dossier explicitly says otherwise. Evidence and planning state remains outside customer work data and grants no implementation credit.

Every user-authored long form uses the universal checkpoint and draft authority. Every canonical workspace mutation uses expected revision, MutationID, one canonical writer transaction, durable receipt, semantic reversal or supersession, and effect-before-receipt recovery. Nonpersistent tooling, views, operating-system presentation, and explicitly device-local preferences instead use their declared idempotency and lifecycle contract; they never fabricate a workspace receipt. No optimistic UI may claim Saved, Complete, Sent, Delivered, Verified, Secure, or Approved beyond the accepted canonical fact.

#### Repository hydration and write fence

P00-C05 derives exact current paths, symbols, declaration, writer and lifecycle owners, tests, generated artifacts, and exclusions from the accepted repository into `HydratedCardExecutionSpecV2`. Dynamic Type through AX5, VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control where relevant, keyboard and error focus, contrast, Reduce Motion, locale and RTL, offline use, permission denial, protected-data lock, storage pressure, cancellation, and relaunch have truthful outcomes. No customer or work data enters telemetry, marketing, advertising, or dormant research systems.

`V23-P00-C04-G01` is Golden, `V23-P00-C04-A01` Alternate, `V23-P00-C04-H01` Hostile, `V23-P00-C04-I01` Interruption, and `V23-P00-C04-R01` Recovery. #### Owned delta and constraints

Define LocalPartDefinition, bounded shop/vehicle/kit/other storage labels, append-only opening/count/adjust/use/return/transfer movements, exact decimal quantity units, derived balance/attention projections, audited abandonment, and atomic work-resource linkage. Parts are not Assets; stock locations are not Sites; locator namespaces never collide. Balance is UNKNOWN until opening/count. Adjustment requires KNOWN; use requires sufficient KNOWN source. Return is provenance-bound by StockReturnAgainstUseReceiptV1 to one exact prior Use movement/receipt, same part/unit/work lineage, positive quantity no greater than its CAS-protected outstanding unreturned frontier, and a KNOWN destination; free-form positive correction is Adjustment, never Return. Transfer requires both sides KNOWN; none treats UNKNOWN as zero or silently creates negative KNOWN. Ordinary retirement requires known-zero everywhere; `ABANDON_UNVERIFIED_STOCK` archives with an immutable unknown-quantity disposition and never asserts zero or loss. Renames never rewrite history, and use/return/reversal updates stock plus the frozen work-resource successor atomically and idempotently. Exclude vendors, purchasing, POs, valuation, tax, invoicing, serialized lots, reservations, cloud, and replenishment automation.
